name: Kalter Schlag
description: Kalter Schlag (Cold Stroke) is a traditional trick-taking game from Hamburg, Germany, closely related to the 'Ramsch' variants of Skat. Played with 32 cards by four players, it is an 'avoidance' game where the objective is to earn as few points as possible. The name refers to the sudden loss that can occur when a player's hand 'cools' or a surprise mistake leads to a massive point capture.

content.text: Kalter Schlag (Cold Stroke) is a traditional trick-taking game from Hamburg, Germany, closely related to the 'Ramsch' variants of Skat. Played with 32 cards by four players, it is an 'avoidance' game where the objective is to earn as few points as possible. The name refers to the sudden loss that can occur when a player's hand 'cools' or a surprise mistake leads to a massive point capture.
Developed as a social variant of Skat and Schafkopf in Northern Germany. It is specifically identified with the pub culture of Hamburg and the surrounding regions.
32 cards (7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each suit).

items.text: Augenramsch: A very similar variant with slightly different Jack rankings.
Schieberamsch: A version where the 'Skats' (extra cards) are passed between players.
Hamburg Standard: The specific 2000-point limit variant.
